- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and supply net is large negative, model tends to undercorrect — force upward adjustment in forecast mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overreacts and continues upward trend — cap growth rate at 2–3% per day post-spike.
- In high-bearish event windows (bearish > 30%), model underestimates downside risk — add 1–2% downward bias to 30d forecast mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model fails to recognize mean reversion — apply slight upward bias to offset overcorrection.
- When official event count is high and supply net is negative, model often ignores event impact — increase forecast volatility by 10–20% to reflect uncertainty.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while true outcome shows sharp decline, model is lagging — adjust forecast to match recent 5-day true trend.
- In multi-event periods (e.g., 15+ events/30d), model tends to overestimate bullishness — reduce forecast slope by 15–25% to reflect event fatigue.
